title: Tollkeeper's Receipt
summary: Act I unique Warrior handaxe dropped by Briar Hounds, pairing Body and accuracy with early lifesteal.
infobox: Briar Hound (Act 1 · M01), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Every kill drops 3 extra gold, but each swing that misses deducts 2 gold from your pouch.
Recovered from the burned toll house at the Sunken Ford. Collector Harlon kept his books balanced in ink until the highland raiders arrived, and in marrow thereafter.
Recovered from the burned toll house at Sunken Ford.
Collector Vance kept his books in ink until raiders came, and in marrow after.

Clerk Brann kept this notched woodcutter's axe under his desk at Alder Ford for travelers who tried to dispute the bridge tariff. When the hounds overran the tollhouse, one carried it off by the leather wrist-loop. Its flat still bears a faint wax-stamp.

title: Bren's Only Dry Boot
summary: Act I unique all-class leather boots from questing, granting brisk speed, poison resistance, and extra health.

p: Grants +25% movement speed in water or mud, but leaves a loud squelching trail that increases enemy aggro range by 3 tiles.
Scout Bren swore he lost its twin in the willow sinks east of Ravenwatch. In truth, he traded it to a bog hermit for three dry biscuits and a map that was mostly lies.
Scout Bren swore he lost its twin in the willow sinks east of Ravenwatch.
In truth, he traded it for three dry biscuits and a lying map.

Ford-Scout Bren swore a soldier only needed one dry boot to stay sane in the northern drizzle, provided he kept switching which foot suffered. The left sole is patched with boiled harness leather and smells strongly of mutton tallow and fen-mud.

title: Candle of the Sunken Sanctum
summary: Act I unique Mage willow wand dropped by Ash-Tongue Shamans, boosting Mind, maximum mana, and fire resistance.
infobox: Ash-Tongue Shaman (Act 1 · M03), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Fire spells deal +20% damage, but standing in water extinguishes the wand for 6 s, reducing spell damage by 15%.
Carved from bleached alder wood and dipped in rendered tallow from the Ravenwatch crypts. Mordred the Ashen used it to light rituals where dry kindling refused to catch.
Bleached alder dipped in crypt tallow that lights where dry kindling fails.

Carved from a willow root pulled out of the flooded sanctum and dipped repeatedly in consecrated tallow until it held a steady, greasy sheen. Hedge-casters argue over whether the wax protects the wood from rot or merely keeps the wielder's fingers from blistering.

title: Splinter of the Bailey
summary: Act I unique Warrior buckler dropped by Quill Fiends, offering sturdy armor, extra health, and a Body bonus.
infobox: Quill Fiend (Act 1 · M03), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Blocks 40% of ranged projectile damage, but burns for double duration when hit by fire.
A three-inch slab of seasoned iron-oak pried from the shattered inner portcullis of Ravenwatch Keep. Three broken iron arrowheads are still wedged in the grain.
Iron-oak pried from Ravenwatch's portcullis, still studded with arrowheads.

Hacked straight out of the shattered oak planking of Ravenwatch's inner gate after the night raid broke the hinges. Someone bolted a bent iron strap to the back and called it a shield. Two broken quill-tips remain wedged permanently in the grain.

title: Tax-Collector's Recurve
summary: Act I unique Archer ash shortbow from Gloom Stags, delivering sharp accuracy, critical chance, and movement speed.
infobox: Gloom Stag (Act 1 · M06), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Every 4th arrow pins the target's shadow to the dirt, rooting them for 2.5 s.
Quartermaster Tarn confiscated forty such bows from Greywood poachers before the war. When the border collapsed, he handed them back with instructions to shoot anything wearing furs.
Confiscated from Greywood poachers, then reissued to shoot anything in furs.

Confiscated three times by Thornwick bailiffs and stolen back from the evidence shed four times by the same unnamed hunter. The limb is rubbed dark with walnut oil so it never catches moonlight, and the grip fits a calloused thumb like an old grudge.

title: Quarryman's Grievance
summary: Act I unique Warrior spiked cudgel dropped by Flintbacks, providing heavy Body, armor, and maximum health.
infobox: Flintback (Act 1 · M01), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Hits against armored or stone targets deal +35% crushing damage and reduce their armor by 2 for 5 s.
Bound with quarry-chain and weighted with a chunk of enchanted granite chipped from Krag Ironhide's left knee. It is unsubtle, poorly balanced, and thoroughly persuasive.
Weighted with chipped granite from a troll's knee; unsubtle and persuasive.

Originally a quarryman's tamping maul studded with horse-shoe nails after the Salt Tithe took the village's real iron. It is too clumsy for polite fencing, yet one solid swing against a shield-boss usually settles any wage dispute on the spot.

title: Seal of Unread Dispatches
summary: Act I unique all-class copper band found in chests, boosting speed, mana regeneration, and cold resistance.

p: While below 35% HP, your movement speed increases by 30%, but you cannot cast offensive spells.
Courier Corin swallowed this signet ring twice during the siege of Lantern Passage to keep it from the Ravine Warden. He politely declined to wear it again afterward.
Courier Corin swallowed this signet twice at Lantern Passage to save his orders.

Worn by courier Corin to stamp wax seals on urgent dispatches that nobody in the capital ever bothered to open. The copper has turned green along the inner rim from three winters of rain, yet the band still hums with restless haste.

title: Miner's Canary Cage
summary: Act I unique Warrior iron helm dropped by Mire Wisps, granting solid armor, high poison resistance, and health.
infobox: Mire Wisp (Act 1 · M02), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Emits a loud metallic chirping whenever poison clouds are within 6 tiles, granting +15% accuracy to nearby allies.
Worn by the deep-sappers who cleared the Undervault Links. There is no bird inside the iron crest anymore—only a bound marsh-wisp that shrieks when the air turns sour.
A bound marsh-wisp inside the crest shrieks whenever mine air turns sour.

A battered dwarven miner's pot-helm fitted with a wire bracket over the brow where a tiny tin cage once hung. The canary is long gone, but the oiled cloth lining still filters out marsh gas and damp cellar rot.

title: Widow's Loom-Weight
summary: Act I unique all-class bloodstone pendant from the Silk Widow, granting high health, poison resistance, and lifesteal.
infobox: Morvessa, the Silk Widow (Act 1 · M11), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: When struck in melee, weaves a brittle silk thread that slows the attacker by 30% for 4 s.
Cut from the calcified silk-gland of Morvessa beneath the Weeping Ossuary. It remains unpleasantly sticky in humid weather and attracts cellar spiders.
Cut from Morvessa's calcified silk-gland; still clammy in damp weather.

Heavy as a merchant's assay weight and hung on a braided cord of dark, unbleached silk. Quartermasters who recognize the stamp on the clasp lower their voices, remembering how neatly its former owner balanced blood against silver.

title: Deserter's Tin Canteen
summary: Act II unique all-class bronze locket dropped by Sand Raiders, offering high health, fire resistance, and Body.
infobox: Sand Raider (Act 2 · M12), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Drinking a Healing Draught also restores 25 mana, but inflicts a 3 s coughing fit that reduces accuracy by 4.
Half-full of Redmarsh brackish water and cheap apricot spirit. It tastes of rust and dead beetles, yet men have killed their brothers at Highgate Watch for a single swallow.
Tastes of rust and dead beetles, yet men killed for a sip at Highgate Watch.

Hammered flat from a dented imperial canteen by a deserter who decided metal over his heart was worth more than warm brine. Shaking it still produces a faint rattle of dry salt crystals sealed inside the soldered seam.

title: Saelen's Marrow-Needle
summary: Act II unique all-class steel rondel dropped by Fen Hexers, pairing high accuracy and critical chance with lifesteal.
infobox: Fen Hexer (Act 2 · M15), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Every critical hit steals 8 mana from the target and infects them with 4 poison damage per second for 6 s.
Hexer Saelen maintained that bloodletting cured all frontier complaints, particularly the complaint of imperial soldiers standing upright in his desert.
Hexer Saelen claimed bloodletting cured enemy soldiers of standing upright.

Hexer Saelen filed this narrow dagger from a broken apothecary's probe, using it to bleed bitter roots and careless travelers alike. The blade is stained dark near the bolster and slides between leather laces without making a sound.

title: Indenture Breaker
summary: Act II unique Warrior heavy morningstar from Pale Burrowers, granting Body, accuracy, and extra maximum health.
infobox: Pale Burrower (Act 2 · M20), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Every 4th hit releases a shockwave of ironstone dust that blinds enemies in a 2-tile radius for 3 s.
Wielded by the head convict of the Deep Quarry during the terrace uprising. The iron chain wrapping the haft is still stamped with his prison serial number.
Its iron-wrapped haft still bears the convict leader's quarry serial number.

Forged from melted debtor shackles in the Deep Quarry after a shift-boss pushed his luck one lash too far. The iron head is ugly, lopsided, and heavy enough to split a basalt block or a turnkey's skull with equal ease.

title: Splinter of the Third Monolith
summary: Act II unique Mage quartz focus dropped by Dune Scarabs, boosting Mind, maximum mana, and high lightning resistance.
infobox: Dune Scarab (Act 2 · M13), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Casting an Air or Earth spell discharges a static arc to the nearest foe within 5 tiles for 18 lightning damage.
Chipped from the northern wardstone during the great dust-rupture. It smells permanently of scorched sand and makes the bearer's hair stand on end before rain.
Chipped from the north monolith; smells of scorched sand and static storm.

Knocked loose from the third plateau monolith when the climate wards fractured under alkali storm-pressure. It tingles faintly against the palm and smells of sharp ozone whenever clouds gather over Redmarsh.

title: Iron Wheel of Wagon Four
summary: Act II unique Warrior iron shield from questing, delivering solid armor, high health, and lightning resistance.

p: Reduces movement speed by 8%, but makes the bearer completely immune to knockback and stun effects.
When the fourth munitions wagon broke its axle in the Redmarsh mire, Quartermaster Bram bolted a leather strap to the iron-rimmed wheel and told his sergeant to stop complaining.
Quartermaster Bram strapped leather to a broken wagon wheel and called it armor.

When Wagon Four snapped its axle in the Ochre Ditch, Quartermaster Bram ordered the iron-rimmed wheel bolted to a spare saddle-strap so the teamsters had cover. It is absurdly heavy, smells of wagon grease, and stops hornbow shafts cold.

title: Spurs of Tactical Withdrawal
summary: Act II unique all-class tracker treads dropped by Dune Lurkers, granting high speed, armor, and accuracy.
infobox: Dune Lurker (Act 2 · M14), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Moving away from enemies grants +20% speed and +4 mana regen, but moving toward them reduces your armor by 2.
Taken from Commander Vorn's baggage train in Spearwind Gorge. His officers called it a rout; his memoirs, left unfinished in the saddlebag, called it 'an aggressive rearward realignment.'
Vorn's officers called it a rout; his memoirs called it rearward realignment.

Fitted with blunt bronze spurs that point slightly inward so a scout can kick free of soft alkali crust without losing his boots. Their original owner insisted he never fled a battle—he merely repositioned aggressively toward the rear.

title: pitch-steeped Winding Sheet
summary: Act II unique Mage weaver robe dropped by Crypt Embalmers, adding Mind, maximum mana, and high poison resistance.
infobox: Crypt Embalmer (Act 2 · M16), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Grants +100% resistance to poison and disease, but increases all fire damage taken by 35%.
Unwound from a three-century-old magistrate in the salt tombs below Redmarsh. The bitumen preservative keeps out marsh-rot wonderfully, provided one stays far from open torches.
Bitumen-soaked burial cloth that keeps out rot if kept far from open flame.

Cut from Third-Dynasty burial linen steeped in dark bitumen and bitter myrrh until the weave turned stiff as oilcloth. It rustles like dry parchment when you walk, yet marsh venom and crypt-spores slide right off the hem.

title: Salt-Mirage Longbow
summary: Act II unique Archer recurve bow dropped by Dune Beasts, combining high accuracy, critical chance, and fire resistance.
infobox: Dune Beast (Act 2 · M12), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Arrows fired from more than 6 tiles away split into a shimmering heat-haze, hitting a second target for 50% damage.
Laminated from dried dune-beast horn and sinew cured in alkaline brine. Looking along the arrow-shelf for too long induces a mild, pleasant hallucination of cold beer.
Sinew-cured horn that makes archers hallucinate cold ale along the arrow-shelf.

Seasoned over Redmarsh salt-pans until the horn belly warped into a wicked, shimmering curve. Marksmen claim aiming down its stave cuts right through noon heat-haze, letting an arrow find a crouching raider before he blinks.

title: Bezoar of the Sand Glutton
summary: Act II unique all-class stone charm from the Sand Glutton, granting high health, armor, and strong poison resistance.
infobox: Gorrathul, the Sand Glutton (Act 2 · M23), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Absorbs the first 15 points of damage from any poison or acid attack and converts it into 10 HP.
Hacked from the third stomach of Gorrathul alongside six rusted belt buckles, a brass astrolabe, and the guild-signet of a missing spice caravan.
Hacked from Gorrathul's third stomach beside six buckles and a guild signet.

A smooth, fist-sized lump of mineral salt and swallowed ironstone pried from the cistern guardian's chest-plate. It stays oddly cold in blistering desert heat and turns aside venoms that would drop a mule in ten paces.

title: Healer Sera's Amputation Saw
summary: Act III unique Warrior flamberge from questing, pairing Body and high critical chance with strong lifesteal.

p: Critical hits inflict a bleeding wound for 8 damage/s over 5 s and heal the nearest injured ally for 20 HP.
'Hold him down and give him the leather strap to bite. If he dies of shock, at least he won't die of gangrene.' — Chief Healer Sera, during the third night at the woodland infirmary.
Bite the leather strap; dying of shock beats dying of marsh gangrene.

Chief Healer Sera never meant for her heavy surgical saw to be swung in anger, yet when raiders rushed the infirmary tents, she worked with what was clean. The wavy teeth tear through mail links with grim, clinical efficiency.

title: Barnacle-Crusted Brigandine
summary: Act III unique all-class hardened brigandine dropped by Salt Crabs, granting high armor, cold resistance, and health.
infobox: Salt Crab (Act 3 · M12), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Attackers striking you in melee take 9 physical thorn damage from the razor-sharp sea barnacles.
Worn by the Sunken Citadel's castellan, who refused to abandon the lower guardroom even after the winter tides permanently claimed the ground floor.
Worn by a castellan who refused to leave even after winter tides took the floor.

Dredged from the flooded courtyard of the Sunken Citadel with a crust of pale sea-barnacles still cemented to the shoulders. Scraping them off ruins the lacquer, and besides, the rough shells catch boarding blades surprisingly well.

title: The Baron's Cooking-Ledger Ring
summary: Act III unique all-class scribe ring found in chests, boosting Mind, maximum mana, and critical strike chance.

p: Shop prices in towns are reduced by 15%, but enemies focus their attacks on you first as if you owed them back-pay.
The rogue baron of Oakhaven kept two signet rings: one for signing imperial tax charters, and this one for transferring garrison pension funds into his private catacombs.
Oakhaven's baron kept this second seal solely to siphon garrison pensions.

Baron Vane kept two signets: a dull pewter one for tax collectors, and this gleaming silver band for his private smuggling tallies. The underside is hollowed out slightly, just deep enough to hide a pinch of cipher-dust.

title: Turnkey of the North Gate
summary: Act III unique Archer heavy arbalest dropped by Hollow Knights, adding high accuracy, critical chance, and Body.
infobox: Hollow Knight (Act 3 · M24), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Fires heavy iron bolts that pierce through the first target to hit a second foe behind them for 75% damage.
When Gate Warden Lyra ran out of standard cedar quarrels during the Hourglass siege, her engineers began loading iron door-hinges and broken jail keys into the windlass.
When cedar bolts ran dry, Warden Lyra's crew loaded iron hinges and jail keys.

The iron stirrup is bent from being slammed into a jammed gate-gear during the retreat from Oakhaven's northern watch. Even crooked, its heavy steel prod punches clean through plate at sixty paces without a tremor.

title: Sluice-Master's Wrench
summary: Act III unique Warrior steel warhammer dropped by Silt Colossi, offering high Body, armor, and lightning resistance.
infobox: Silt Colossus (Act 3 · M37), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Every 5th hit knocks the target backward 2 tiles and stuns them for 2 s.
Fourteen pounds of drop-forged Oakhaven iron designed to turn the rusted floodgate gears of Riverlock Crossing. It turns helmets with equal mechanical leverage.
Drop-forged to turn rusted canal gears; it turns helmets with equal leverage.

Unbolted from the central canal floodgate when the lock-keeper ran out of pikes and decided forty pounds of greased iron worked better. The squared socket still fits a sluice-pin, though nowadays it mostly dents helmets.

title: Lightning-Split Bough
summary: Act III unique Mage rune staff dropped by Stormtrees, granting high Mind, large mana reserves, and mana regeneration.
infobox: Stormtree (Act 3 · M37), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Chain Lightning and Thunderstorm jump to 2 additional targets, but each cast shocks the wielder for 6 HP.
Harvested from the charred heartwood of the coastal Stormtree. The wood never truly stopped burning; it merely agreed to wait until pointed at someone else.
Charred coastal heartwood that never stopped burning, only waited for a target.

Split straight from the smoking heartwood of a lightning-struck coastal pine where sap cooked into glowing yellow glass. Holding it makes the hair on your forearms rise, and spells leap from its tip with a dry crack.

title: Harbor-Burner's Astrolabe
summary: Act III unique Mage spell-mirror dropped by Ash Weavers, adding Mind, accuracy, and strong fire resistance.
infobox: Ash Weaver (Act 3 · M43), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Increases the reach of all ranged spells by +2 tiles.
Taken from Admiral Kael's charred cabin aboard his flagship in Harborwatch. The brass lenses are cracked by heat, yet they still calculate artillery trajectories with cruel precision.
Heat-cracked brass lenses that still reckon broadside arcs with cruel precision.

Salvaged from the scorched quarterdeck of a fire-ship outside Harborwatch, its brass rings warped slightly by burning pitch. Casters peer through the smoked lens to sight distant targets cleanly through thick harbor smoke.

title: Clapper of the Submerged Nave
summary: Act III unique Mage astral medallion dropped by Frost Bells, providing high mana, cold resistance, and mana regeneration.
infobox: Frost Bell (Act 3 · M26), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Whenever your mana drops below 20%, emits a freezing chime that slows all foes within 4 tiles for 4 s (30 s cooldown).
A salt-eaten bronze pendulum salvaged from the flooded bell-tower of the Sunken Citadel. Even on dry land, it swings slightly in rhythm with the coastal tide.
Salvaged from the flooded nave; it still swings in rhythm with coastal tides.

A corroded bronze clapper pulled from a submerged abbey nave where the tide rings the bells twice a day. Hung on a wool cord, it stays wet with phantom spray and hums a steady, cold note that keeps mana flowing.

title: Hollow Reed of Vesperion
summary: Act III unique Mage crystal siphon wand from Vesperion, delivering high Mind, large mana, and potent lifesteal.
infobox: Vesperion, the Hollow Choir (Act 3 · M45), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Spells drain 5 mana from every enemy hit and restore it to the caster.
One of the smaller bone pipes from Vesperion's dorsal cathedral organ. When swung through the air, it produces a flat, liturgical F-sharp that makes dogs weep.
A bone pipe from Vesperion's organ whose flat F-sharp makes watchdogs weep.

Cut from a tarnished silver reed-pipe that once droned across the black blockade's flagship. In a caster's hand, it drinks both breath and vitality from nearby foes, whistling softly whenever a spell lands true.

title: Malrik's Margin-Notes
summary: Act IV unique Mage cosmos eye dropped by Rift Moths, granting top Mind, massive mana, and high mana regeneration.
infobox: Rift Moth (Act 4 · M37), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Reduces all spell cooldowns by 20%, but 15% of all damage taken is subtracted from your Mana before HP.
Bound in the fire-cured hide of a highland drake. Arch-Mage Malrik's handwriting begins in neat academic script and degenerates over three hundred pages into frantic geometric diagrams.
Malrik's neat Collegium notes degenerate into frantic caldera diagrams.

Stuffed with cramped, furious margin-notes written in violet ink by a scholar who stopped believing in Collegium patience. Even half-charred from caldera sparks, the pages hum with disciplined, ruthless arcane arithmetic.

title: Dent of Greystone Wall
summary: Act IV unique Warrior dread crest helm dropped by Basalt Brutes, offering high armor, health, and fire resistance.
infobox: Basalt Brute (Act 4 · M36), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Reduces damage from area-of-effect explosions and boulders by 45%.
Captain Rowan took a glancing blow from a basalt catapult stone on the third day at Greystone Bastion. His neck was never straight again, which he claimed improved his posture on parade.
Dented by a basalt stone at Greystone; Rowan claimed it improved his posture.

Bears a deep, palm-wide furrow across the left temple where a siege-stone glanced off during the defense of Greystone Wall. Captain Rowan refused to let the smith hammer the dent out, claiming it reminded him to keep his chin down.

title: Tongs of the Cinderforge
summary: Act IV unique Warrior obsidian greatmaul dropped by Anvilmaw Smiths, pairing top Body with fire resistance and critical chance.
infobox: Anvilmaw Smith (Act 4 · M38), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Every 3rd hit brands the target with white-hot slag, dealing 15 fire damage/s for 4 s and melting 3 armor.
Still glowing dull cherry-red at the core. If left on a wooden table in Ironcamp, it burns its way through to the floorboards before the ale goes flat.
Still cherry-red at the core; it chars oak tables before the ale goes flat.

Wrenched from the cooling fingers of a cinderforge titan and lashed to an ironwood shaft with braided chain. The head still radiates a dull, dry warmth that chars leather straps and leaves smoking dents in basalt plate.

title: Caldera Glass Greatbow
summary: Act IV unique Archer windpiercer greatbow from Redglass Drakes, delivering top accuracy, critical chance, and speed.
infobox: Redglass Drake (Act 4 · M36), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Arrows shatter into volcanic glass on impact, dealing 30% of their damage in a 2-tile cone behind the target.
Ribbed with flexible strips of crimson obsidian taken from a Redglass Drake's wing-spar. Drawing the string without heavy leather gauntlets is a quick way to lose three fingers.
Ribbed with crimson obsidian that slices bare fingers on a careless draw.

Laminated with thin splinters of volcanic redglass that flex without snapping in freezing highland drafts. Arrows loosed from its string hiss like hot iron plunged into a trough, striking before the target hears the draw.

title: Portcullis of the First Checkpoint
summary: Act IV unique Warrior citadel aegis dropped by Dread Knights, offering top armor, high health, and fire and lightning resistance.
infobox: Dread Knight (Act 4 · M39), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: While standing completely still, you gain +5 armor and reflect 25% of ranged damage back at the shooter.
Carried through the Gauntlet of Iron by a vanguard sergeant who died standing upright, wedged so tightly between two basalt boulders that the enemy had to climb over him.
Its bearer died wedged upright in the pass so his company could climb over.

Forged from a melted iron portcullis after the First Checkpoint collapsed under mortar fire. Carrying it feels like hauling a cellar door uphill, yet nothing short of a direct caldera tremor can push its bearer back.

title: Coal-Walker's Sabatons
summary: Act IV unique Warrior war greaves dropped by Cinderhorns, granting high armor, massive fire resistance, and speed.
infobox: Cinderhorn (Act 4 · M42), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Leaves a trail of burning embers as you walk that deals 10 fire damage/s to pursuing enemies, but burns you for 2 HP/s while standing still.
Forged without leather linings so they would never catch fire in the lava trenches of the Outer Rampart. The soldiers who wore them learned never to stop marching.
Forged without leather linings so soldiers in lava trenches never stopped marching.

Lined with woven mineral cloth and thick iron soles studded with blunt nails for gripping hot volcanic scree. Scorched Penitents wore them across glowing slag trenches to prove their faith; sensible soldiers wear them to keep their toes.

title: Abdication
summary: Act IV unique Warrior zweihander dropped by Hollow Kings, combining high Body, lifesteal, critical chance, and cold resistance.
infobox: Hollow King (Act 4 · M29), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Deals +25% damage to bosses and elite monsters, and executes non-boss enemies below 12% HP instantly.
An ancient coronation greatsword whose royal crest was chiseled off with a cold iron punch. It weighs as much as a wet sack of salt and cuts like a broken treaty.
Coronation steel with its royal crest chiseled off; cuts like a broken treaty.

A long, joyless greatsword stripped of every royal crest with a coarse iron file. Its balance sits heavy toward the point, built for sweeping aside entire ranks of retainers who still mistake a crown for authority.

title: Signet of the Two Paths
summary: Act IV unique all-class vigor signet from questing, granting balanced Body, Mind, maximum health, and maximum mana.

p: When HP is above 50%, grants +15% spell damage; when HP is below 50%, grants +15% physical damage and +8% lifesteal.
Found upon the stone threshold before the Crown Vault. One half of the bezel is set with cold celestial silver, the other with slag from the Obsidian Throne.
One half set in cold silver, the other in slag from the Obsidian Dais.

Cast from twin strands of cold silver and blackened caldera iron twisted tightly around a blank central seal. Archivists note that the metal feels neither warm nor cold until its wearer finally chooses which road to walk.

title: Cinder-King's Halberd-Horn
summary: Act IV unique all-class spire medallion from the Cinder King, boosting Mind, Body, massive fire resistance, and critical chance.
infobox: Ashkarath, the Cinder King (Act 4 · M46), Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble

p: Every 5th spell or weapon attack unleashes a ring of volcanic fire around you for 38 fire damage.
A molten iron sword-tip broken from the blazing halo above Ashkarath's brow. Even suspended on a heavy chain, it pulls slightly toward the center of the earth.
A molten horn-tip from Ashkarath's halo that pulls toward the earth's core.

Snapped from the jagged crest of an ancient furnace-crown and pierced with a simple iron wire so a mortal can wear it without blistering. It pulses with a slow, steady heat like a banked forge waiting for fresh bellows.

title: Fen-Poacher's Yew

p: Silent draw wrapped in oiled otter-pelt.
Stripped from a border poacher who fed three Thornwick taverns on crown venison before the bridge wardens caught him.
Silent draw wrapped in oiled otter-pelt for wet reed-beds.

Cut from a stunted churchyard yew leaning over the Fenwick boundary ditch, seasoned in peat-smoke for two winters. Poachers swear it shoots quieter than ash, letting a hunter loose twice before the gamekeeper's dogs catch the scent.

title: Toll-Tower Prod

infobox: Act 2 Bosses, Super-Uniques, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (Smart Grail Pity at 25%)

p: Horn-tipped limbs notched for bridge-post distance markers.
Issued to Redmarsh toll-marksmen who collected tariffs from forty paces across the dry salt-beds.
Horn-tipped limbs notched for exact bridge-post distance markers.

Built to shoot cleanly from narrow stone arrow-slits across wide river fords and canyon mouths. The stiff limbs punish weak wrists, yet a seasoned marksman can pick a driver off a wagon seat before the horses reach the gate.

title: Bracken Wind-Reader
summary: Tier-3 Act III unique Archer composite bow from bosses and bounties, boosting damage, critical chance, and attack speed.

p: Sinew-backed limbs lacquered against coastal squalls.
Carried by Fen-Warden Hale through forty dust storms without a single warped nock or snapped string.
Sinew-backed limbs lacquered thick against Redmarsh squalls.

Backed with pale desert horn and wrapped in oil-stained linen to keep out coastal spray. Scouts who survived Bracken Basin carved tiny wind-notches along the riser so they could adjust their aim by touch in the dark.

title: Harborwall Winch-Arbalest
summary: Tier-4 Act IV unique Archer heavy arbalest from bosses and bounties, delivering high damage, armor penetration, and crit damage.

p: Steel prod stamped with Oakhaven's customs anchor.
Spanned with a belt-hook to punch iron quarrels clean through smuggler hull-planks at low tide.
Heavy steel prod stamped with Oakhaven's customs anchor.

Salvaged from Oakhaven's outer seawall batteries and cut down to a stock a broad-shouldered trooper can actually carry. Winding the steel cord takes grit, yet its heavy bolts crack stone golems like dried walnuts.
